bounds: CONSUMER-ONLY: this lane codes against the FROZEN protocol in lane-s-change-feed.md §3.2; the route itself is Lane S's deliverable and was NOT run here, so nothing in this evidence claims the server emits a frame. Every arm feeds the frame into a fake EventSource by hand.

The EventSource double models ONLY the two members the view may touch (onmessage, close) plus an onerror the view never installs. It does NOT model the browser's own reconnect/retry, nor that a closed stream delivers nothing further — so 'no read after close' is the browser's guarantee, not an assertion of these arms.

The transport is not exercised: no HTTP, no chunked transfer, no proxy. The harness's fetch double is a plain function and there is no gzip/compression layer anywhere in this lane's plumbing (no `gzip`/`compress` match under packages/mpd-bundle-plugin/src or packages/mpd-dsh-adapter-plugin/src); whether the HOST's http server buffers text/event-stream is Lane S's acceptance subject (lane-s §3.2 requires the handler to opt the stream out), and it is invisible from the browser artifact.

The elapsed 3 ms is the offline settle (two macrotasks), not a network round trip; the <200 ms budget is therefore proven for the CLIENT path only (a frame that arrives is a read immediately), never for end-to-end latency.
The interval double removes the timer, so the arms prove the frame's read did not come from the interval; they do not measure how often a real browser fires the 2000 ms interval.

W-d: the web vocabulary duplicate is DECLARED, not removed; today's 6/6 agreement is a measurement of this tree, not a guarantee — only a future build-time derivation (or a cross-package test) would make a drift fail.
